passages.title: The little duck
passages.text: Dot is a small yellow duck. She loves the pond. Every morning she swims in circles and quacks hello to the frogs.

questions.q: What does she do every morning?
options: Swims and says hello to the frogs

passages.title: A rainy day
passages.text: It rained all afternoon. Sam put on his red boots and jumped in the puddles. Later, his dad was waiting with a towel and hot soup.

questions.q: Who was waiting with a towel?

passages.title: Bees
passages.text: Bees live in hives and work as a team. They visit flowers to collect nectar, which they turn into honey. While flying from flower to flower they carry pollen, which helps new plants grow.

questions.q: What do bees turn into honey?

passages.title: The 7:10 train
passages.text: Maya got to the station at a quarter to seven. Her train left at ten past seven. She sat on a bench and read her book while she waited.

questions.q: What time did Maya get to the station?
How many minutes did she wait for the train?

passages.title: Roman numerals
passages.text: The Romans wrote numbers with letters: I is 1, V is 5, X is 10, L is 50 and C is 100. To write 14 they used XIV, which means 10 plus 5 minus 1. We still see these numbers on some clocks and in the names of certain kings.

questions.q: What is the value of the letter X?
Where do we still see these numbers?
options: On clocks and in kings' names

passages.title: A little every day
passages.text: A coach used to say that practicing a little every day is worth more than practicing a lot on a single day. The brain, like a muscle, grows stronger with repetition. That is why fifteen minutes of mental math every day for a year adds up to more than ninety hours of training.

questions.q: According to the text, what is worth more?
options: Practicing a lot on one day
